title: The Provision of the Empty Quarter
premise: Orsen Ashgrove flies supplies into a remote mountain interior where the government survey team he's been ferrying vanishes without tracks, leaving behind gear that suggests they walked into the range on purpose. Pressured by an official who wants the disappearance buried and haunted by the team's last radio call naming him, Orsen crosses the high passes ahead of the snows with a survivor who shouldn't exist — the surveyor's daughter traveling under a false name. The truth: the team found evidence of a covered-up contamination site, and the 'vanishing' was an extraction gone wrong. In the calving season's brief window, Orsen must choose between loyalty to the people who kept him flying and exposing the truth that will cost him his license and his anonymity; he chooses truth, crash-lands the evidence out of the range, and finally stops moving.
about_author: Paloma Blackwood is the pen name of a former bush pilot turned novelist who spent six years flying freight across northern ranges before trading the cockpit for a writing desk. Her fiction draws on real flight logs, vanished expeditions, and the quiet ethics of people who live where roads don't go.

chapters.title: Fuel, Rumors, Weather
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Establishes his routine: medicine runs, gossip as cargo, debts in three towns, and a rule against staying anywhere longer than a night. He drops supplies at the survey camp and notes something off — too much gear left behind, no one waving him off. Emotional beat: restless competence masking a man avoiding his own past.

chapters.title: The Camp With No Tracks
chapters.summary: Orsen returns on schedule to find the survey camp abandoned: stoves warm, logbooks burned, footprints ending at the tree line. He reports it and is met not with alarm but with smooth reassurance from an official named Corven, who asks oddly specific questions about what Orsen saw. Emotional beat: unease hardening into suspicion.

chapters.title: A Passenger Named Nobody
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, then shifting to Mara, a young woman who charters a flight out but carries survey-team equipment tags sewn into her pack lining. She claims to be a prospector's niece; her hands say otherwise. Orsen doesn't confront her — yet. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's craft.

chapters.title: The Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She reveals she is the lead surveyor's daughter, traveling incognito since her father's final radio message named Orsen by name — a man he'd never met. The message hinted at 'what we found under the ice.' Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose; Orsen realizes he's already implicated.

chapters.title: Corven's Offer
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Corven offers to forgive Orsen's licensing violations and fuel debts if he flies a 'recovery' mission that is clearly a suppression run — burn the camp, lose the records. Orsen stalls, then agrees outwardly while planning otherwise. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal, and hated.

chapters.title: Into the Range Ahead of the Snows
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Orsen and Mara fly in low through deteriorating weather, guided by her father's coded field notes, aiming for a glacier route that opens only briefly during calving season. A near-miss with a ridge forces them down at a frozen lake. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into focus; trust built in turbulence.

chapters.title: What We Found Under the Ice
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. On foot along the glacier, they find the survey team alive but captive-adjacent — hiding from their own government minders, guarding core samples proving contamination upstream of every settlement Orsen serves. The 'vanishing' was self-exile. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed; the enemy was never the wilderness.

chapters.title: The Window Closes
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Corven's recovery team arrives by air; the calving window begins to shut. The surveyors scatter samples among trusted locals, and Orsen volunteers to fly the master cores out alone through weather no sane pilot enters. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth resolved into action — he can't carry both, so he carries the truth.

chapters.title: Calving
chapters.summary: Climax, Orsen's POV. The glacier calves as he lifts off; Corven's plane pursues through the collapsing route. Orsen flies the icefall corridor he swore he'd never attempt, takes damage, and puts the cores down beyond Corven's reach — crashing deliberately short of the strip but within reach of witnesses. Emotional beat: terror, then terrible calm.

chapters.title: The Long Taxi Home
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating POV. The evidence goes public; Corven is undone by the very flight logs he once held over Orsen. Orsen loses his license, gains something rarer — a reason to stay. He repairs the wrecked plane slowly, in one place, with Mara and the town watching. Emotional beat: stillness chosen at last, and found survivable.
